title: Blood flow at rest and in exercise

match.reason: The bank point teaches the structure and roles of arteries, capillaries and veins, not how blood is redistributed from the gut to working muscles during exercise, so it is a different idea.

draft.title: Blood flow at rest and in exercise
card: The body has a limited supply of blood. At rest, a fair share goes to organs such as the digestive system and kidneys, and a smaller share goes to the muscles.
In exercise, the working muscles need more oxygen and fuel. The heart pumps harder, so more blood is moved each minute.
Blood is redirected as well. Vessels supplying working muscles widen, and vessels supplying organs such as the gut narrow, so less blood goes there.
The result is that a much larger share of blood reaches the working muscles during exercise than at rest.
draft.remember: In exercise, the heart pumps more blood and sends a bigger share to the working muscles.

a.q: Compared with rest, what happens to blood flow to the gut during hard exercise?
opts: Its share of blood falls as more goes to muscles
Its share of blood rises to help digest food faster
Its share stays the same because it is an organ
Its blood flow stops completely until exercise ends
a.why: Blood is redirected to working muscles, so the gut gets a smaller share. It does not stop completely, and the body does not raise gut flow to digest food during hard exercise.
a.clue: Think about where the body most needs oxygen during exercise.

b.q: Priya is on a netball court in Geelong and runs hard for ten minutes. Which change in blood flow best explains how her leg muscles get more oxygen?
opts: The heart pumps harder and vessels to her legs widen
The heart slows so blood moves gently through her legs
The heart pumps harder and vessels to her legs narrow
The body makes extra blood so no redirecting is needed
b.why: A harder-working heart moves more blood, and widened vessels let more of it reach her legs. Narrowing the leg vessels would cut supply to the muscles that need it most. The body does not make extra blood in minutes, so redirecting is needed.
b.clue: Working muscles need a bigger share, so what must their vessels do?

a.best: Its share of blood falls as more goes to muscles

b.best: The heart pumps harder and vessels to her legs widen
